display.title: The Slavita Printer, Part 1
display.summary_short: On the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit: a Chassid who needs a printing permit is sent by the Alter Rebbe to fetch a humble teacher and travel to Vilna, where a mysterious official notices them.
display.summary_long: Told on the night of Chof-Daled Teves, the yahrzeit of the Alter Rebbe, after the song 'I believe in Hashem'. Rabbi Moshe, son of the tzaddik Rabbi Pinchas of Koretz, wants to open a printing press because sefarim are scarce in Russia. The storyteller explains the obstacles: government censorship (with an example from Birkas HaMazon and the Rebbe's reply about it), a permit from a minister in Petersburg who hates Jews, and heavy fees. The Alter Rebbe tells him to go to Mogilev, bring along Reb Yisrael, the town's melamed, and travel with him to Vilna. Neither man understands why, but they obey. In Vilna they stay with Reb Meir Refoels, now a devoted Chassid, who knows that the Rebbe's words must be followed exactly. While the three discuss Chassidus on a park bench, an elegantly dressed stranger stops to stare at Reb Yisrael and invites him to his hotel the next morning. Reb Meir recognizes the name on the pass: it is the Minister of Education himself. To be continued next week.
display.lesson: When the Rebbe gives an instruction, follow it exactly even when it does not make sense to us.
